description: The chart illustrates how many tasks are associated with each linguistic family in the “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models” paper. The categories are shown on the vertical axis as language-family labels in descending order of task count: IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque. The horizontal axis is the value axis labeled “# tasks,” shown on a linear scale with tick marks at regular 10-unit intervals from 0 to 80. Each category is represented by a single horizontal bar with a distinct color: IE-Slavic (light blue) extends to just under 80 tasks (approximately 79–80), IE-Romance (dark blue) reaches just under 50 (about 47), IE-Germanic (light green) reaches the mid-40s (about 44), Uralic (green) reaches about 20, IE-Baltic (light pink) reaches about 17, IE-other (red) reaches about 15, IE-Indic (tan/orange) reaches about 10, Semitic (orange-brown) reaches about 8, Turkic (light purple) reaches about 4, and Basque (dark purple) reaches about 3. The bars are not stacked or grouped, there is no legend beyond the bar colors themselves, and no bars appear specially annotated or otherwise emphasized beyond their distinct fills.
caption_used: The bar chart presents the distribution of tasks across various linguistic families, ordered by descending task count. The vertical axis lists the families as IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, while the horizontal axis quantifies the number of tasks on a scale from 0 to 80. IE-Slavic, represented in light blue, dominates with approximately 80 tasks, followed by IE-Romance (dark blue) at roughly 50 tasks. IE-Germanic (light green) stabilizes at around 40 tasks, while Uralic (green) sharply declines to 25 tasks. IE-Baltic (light pink) and IE-other (red) exhibit comparable task counts, each hovering near 18 tasks, with IE-Baltic marginally exceeding IE-other. IE-Indic (orange) and Semitic (brown) demonstrate a modest but consistent gap, with IE-Indic at 12 tasks and Semitic at 8. Turkic (light purple) and Basque (dark purple) round out the distribution, with Turkic registering 7 tasks and Basque approximately 5. The data reveal a pronounced disparity between the top three families and the remaining groups, with IE-Germanic and Uralic forming a transitional plateau before the steep drop-off in task numbers for lower-ranked families.
